In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are not conclusive.
LCs are a natural consequence of training a NN with invariant features, but the conditions required for them to be found are not well understood.
LCs emerge in feed-forward NNs in response to moderately invariant features and that they are robust to perturbations until 40% of the features are changed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that localist coding schemes can be found in feed-forward networks, and that they emerge when invariant features are presented, but they do not emerge when the features become less invariant, or when a network is deep.

the emergence of local codes in feed forward neural networks is a robust phenomenon, which is not dependent on the choice of the architecture or the activation function, but is sensitive to the training conditions.

the local codes are more likely to be found in feed-forward networks if the training data contains invariant features, if the network is allowed to train for longer and if the training data is not too large.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of LCs is a robust feature of feed-forward NNs.
local codes emerge in response to invariant input features.
localist codes emerge in response to invariant stimuli.
